newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed on long liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Monday due to long liquidation after sharp gains in the past few weeks, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 21,250 yuan ($2,560) per tonne, losing 10 yuan. It opened at 21,250 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 21,260 and a low of 21,120.
January rose 40 to 20,590, February 10 to 20,730, March fell 10 to 21,020, May rose 50 to 21,310 and June was unchanged at 21,300.
Combined volume fell sharply to 50,600 tonnes from 133,210.
Copper opened lower and fell further before some speculative buying pushed the contracts off their lows late in the session.
"Long liquidation dominated today's trading, because some investors thought the current futures prices were too high," one trader said.
"Copper has risen a lot during the past few weeks due to improved market sentiment and better technical charts," he added.
Traders said lower spot prices also prevented the contracts from rising further.
"Spot prices can't catch up with futures prices, which has put heavy pressure on investors," a second trader said. The price of Shanghai spot copper is around 20,400 yuan per tonne.
Traders added another reason for today's mixed movement was that many investors preferred to stay on the sidelines with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday.
But some traders said slight falls on thin volume did not change the upward trend in the short term.
"If later-maturing contracts can find strong support at 21,000 yuan level, copper will rise further in the next few days," a third trader said.
Aluminium ended little changed. The only traded January 1997 contract fell 10 yuan to close at 13,950 yuan per tonne on volume of 790 tonnes.
